text:
marco: Following up from the postmortem: recurring long-request bursts hit our dedicated pool again. We need a concise SLO update plan, rollback criteria, and explicit owners for dashboards + runbook.

anya: Agree. We should avoid permanently loosening SLOs. Proposal: temporary p99 guardrail change with clear rollback triggers and acceptance tests. Keep p95 strict.

zach: Quick facts from oncall: peak p99 ~1.85s during the spike, sustained for ~8m. Queue depth on a few instances spiked >180, KV-cache miss jumped to 42%.

oncall-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-390 | Sev2 | start=2175478000 | end=2175482800 | primary=serving-runtime | link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-390

anya: Draft SLO patch (short-term):
```
metric: inference_latency
windows:
  - lookback: 30d
    p95: <= 230ms
  - lookback: 14d
    p99: <= 1.05s  # temporary, review after batching fix
notes: revert p99 to previous target after canary passes and 7d stable telemetry
```
Explainers added to PR.

marco: Rollback criteria (suggested):
- if error_rate attributable to fallback/canary increases >1.5% over baseline for 10m -> auto rollback
- if end-to-end p95 regresses by >20% for 5m -> alert + rollback
- if customer-facing errors (5xx) increase -> immediate rollback
We should include these as CI gates in the canary job.

zach: I'll own the CI gating + perf tests. ETA: 2026-04-03. I'll add an integration sim that mixes 90% small requests with 10% >2k-token to validate batching scheduler changes.

anya: I'll own dashboard + alerting. Plan: new panels for token-size percentile (p50/p90/p99), per-instance queue depth, KV-cache miss rate, and routing fallback rate. Alerts: p99 > 1s for 3m -> page; queue_depth > 150 for 2m -> page; kv_miss > 30% for 5m -> channel. ETA: 2026-04-02.

platform-lead: Approve owners. Add requirement: dashboard must include an error-budget burn chart with daily granularity and a link to the postmortem action tracker. Also add explicit owner field in each alert rule.

marco: Action list recap:
- anya: dashboard + alerts PR with playbook links (due 2026-04-02)
- zach: perf test + CI canary gating (due 2026-04-03)
- marco: SLO PR with rollback criteria + SLO notes (due 2026-04-01)
- platform-lead: schedule canary window and approve perf thresholds (due 2026-04-05)

zach: Question: should the fallback route return a warning header or a structured field so clients can opt-in? I prefer a header first to avoid breaking clients.

anya: Header is safer. We'll add `X-Redwood-Fallback: compact-quant` when fallback is used. Add telemetry tag for sampled outputs so we can QA quality drift.

marco: Also, let's add a one-time error-budget transfer note: if we exceed 50% of the 14d error budget for p99 during the rollback window, we pause non-essential changes until we stabilize. Put that in the postmortem action tracker.

oncall-bot: Reminder created: "Long-context remediation sync" 2026-04-06 10:00 UTC. Attendees: @eng-oncall, @platform-team

platform-lead: I'll also require a short post-canar y report with: perf numbers, error delta, customer-impact summary, and decision (promote/rollback).

marco: Thanks. I'll update the postmortem tracker and ping infra leads for SLO review. If anyone needs to reassign items, flag here. :thumbsup:
